# Balance lookup diagnosis

The client passed only `account` as the pending key. Requests from different tenants for the same account therefore shared one result. A single string joined with a delimiter would also be ambiguous when identifiers contain that delimiter. The client now encodes the ordered `[tenant, account]` pair as a JSON array key and still passes both original strings to `load`.

The pending helper called `load` before registering its Promise. A synchronous throw escaped instead of becoming a rejected Promise, and a reentrant lookup could start duplicate work. It also cleared entries only on fulfillment. Its `then` cleanup created an unhandled rejected Promise when `load` rejected. The helper now registers a Promise before running `load` and clears the entry through both fulfillment and rejection handlers. It keeps no fulfilled cache.

The resolver used `value.balanceMinor || 100`, which replaced a valid zero balance, and hard-coded `USD`, which discarded the returned currency. It now returns the supplied minor units and currency unchanged alongside the requested identifiers. Lookup failures still reject.

## Verification

Run `node --test balance.test.mjs` and `node smoke.mjs`. The regression tests cover tenant and delimiter isolation, shared active Promises, reload after fulfillment and rejection, plain values, synchronous throws, reentrant loading, the existing `singleFlight` export, zero and negative minor units, currency preservation, and error propagation. The rejection test allows an event-loop turn so an extra unhandled rejection is reported by the test runner.

## Causes

- `createBalanceClient` used only `account` as its pending key. Requests from different tenants for the same account therefore shared a result. - `singleFlight` called the loader before wrapping its result, so a synchronous throw escaped instead of returning a rejected Promise. Its pending entry was cleared only on fulfillment. # Checkout incident

## Cause and impact

At 10:04 UTC, payments v2.8 lowered `ledger_pool_limit` from 32 to 4. The ledger trace shows active connections pinned at 4, while all 12 rejected checkouts waited more than 250 ms for a connection and returned 503. This supports a ledger connection-pool limit regression as the cause of the checkout failures. (L0013, L0305)

From 10:05 to 10:08 UTC, 12 of 80 checkout requests returned 503 and 68 succeeded: a 15% observed failure rate. (L0062)

## Rejected hypothesis

On-call initially suspected DNS resolution (L0127), but the resolver audit found that all 80 payments hostname resolutions succeeded, with zero DNS failures. The DNS hypothesis was rejected. (L0214)

## Mitigation and verification

At 10:09 UTC, the ledger pool limit was restored to 32 without changing the hostname, resolver, or application version. From 10:10 to 10:15 UTC, 200 checkouts produced zero 503s and p95 latency was 110 ms. This verifies recovery in the observed post-mitigation window. (L0399, L0488)

## Unknown

Delayed settlement impact remains unknown because no settlement observation was collected. (L0532)

# Checkout incident

Payments v2.8 went live at 10:04 UTC with `ledger_pool_limit=4`, down from 32 in v2.7 (L0013). The supported root cause is the reduced ledger connection pool: all 12 rejected checkouts waited more than 250 ms for a connection, returned 503, and the active connection count was pinned at four (L0305). This links the failures to pool capacity, though the log does not explain why the limit changed.

From 10:05 to 10:08 UTC, 12 of 80 checkout requests returned 503 and 68 succeeded: a 15% observed failure rate (L0062). An initial DNS hypothesis was unverified when raised (L0127) and rejected after an audit found that all 80 payments hostname resolutions succeeded with zero DNS failures (L0214).

At 10:09 UTC, the pool limit was restored to 32 without changing the hostname, resolver, or application version (L0399). From 10:10 to 10:15 UTC, 200 observed checkouts had zero 503 responses and p95 latency was 110 ms (L0488). This supports the pool limit mitigation for the observed window; it does not establish longer term behavior.

Delayed settlement impact remains unknown because no settlement observation was collected (L0532). The log also does not establish whether affected customers retried successfully.
